channel.title: Omarchy Stories
channel.description:
Omarchy Stories — A signal from nowhere.

This is a transmission by the community, for the community.

Omarchy is beautiful, fun & agentic Linux — opinionated by DHH, but yours to command. And behind every install there's a story: the developer who stopped renting their workflow from Cupertino, the tinkerer who vibed their way through an alteration nobody thought possible, the stubborn fix that became community knowledge overnight.

Omarchy Stories broadcasts those people. Each episode is a field report from someone in command — what they escaped, what they changed, what they fixed, and what the next Omarch can learn from it.

No gatekeepers, no marketing filter, no permission required.

If you have an interesting Omarchy story, this is your platform.

Because that's the whole point: when something breaks, nobody here waits for Apple or Microsoft to allow the fix.

Someone finds it. Someone shares it. Everybody moves faster.

The community is the signal. Tune in.

We can fix everything.

item.title: Bjarne Øverli - Omarchy Core Team
item.description:
What makes computing fun again? In episode 004 of Omarchy Stories, Bjarne Øverli joins the conversation to talk about Linux, creative side projects, and finding a community you want to build with.

A self-taught developer, CTO at Unite AS, and member of the Omarchy Core team, Bjarne shares his journey from early Linux and BSD experiments to helping shape Omarchy. We explore the balance between an opinionated setup and the freedom to make your computer your own—and what everyday life on the core team looks like.

We also dig into Thema, CLIAMP, and the appeal of bringing Winamp nostalgia to the terminal. From radio streams and the pirate-radio spirit behind Omarchy Stories to AI in the operating system and meeting fellow builders at Omacon, this episode is about the tools and people that make technology personal.

Bjarne also reflects on learning by doing, finding his own path into the industry, and sharing projects publicly before feeling fully ready.

Follow Omarchy Stories for more conversations with the people building and shaping the community.

item.title: Jankees van Woezik - Omarchy Plugins and Indie Maker
item.description:
Omarchy Stories 003: Jankees van Woezik

In this episode of Omarchy Stories, Basti sits down with Jankees to talk about software development, AI-assisted building, plugins, security, and where coding is headed.

Jankees walks through his path from early web development and system administration into building tools, running a company, and writing plugins for Omarchy. Along the way, the two get into what responsible AI use actually looks like in practice, why taste and fundamentals still matter, how children learn best by experimenting, and how AI might reshape work, education, privacy, and software engineering.

They also cover Omarchy Kids, screen time philosophy, teaching programming to children, building a startup with AI, the developer community, and practical security research.

item.title: Erik Melton - Omarchy Security Team
item.description:
Erik Melton shares his path into software engineering and cybersecurity, and why problem-solving skills matter more than formal education.

He breaks down the complexities of PCI DSS compliance, his move from a highly regulated industry into media, and how the role of code in software engineering is changing. The conversation covers what actually counts in today's job market — preparation, real experience and a strong portfolio — as well as the weight of clear communication and personal connection in the interview process. It closes on the role of trust and community engagement in security-related projects.

item.title: Mehmet Ince - Omarcy Security Team
item.description:
In the first episode of Omarchy Stories, I'm joined by Mehmet Ince from the Omarchy Security Team.

We talk about how he found his way into cybersecurity and what still draws him to vulnerability research — the kind of work where you keep digging until something gives.

Mehmet shares what his role on the security team looks like and how the team works internally: how closely they collaborate, and how much learning happens along the way. We get into the impact of AI on vulnerability research, open source culture, and how vulnerabilities get reported — including what it means when one of them hits the entire Linux ecosystem.

From there we look at the particular challenges in the Postgres ecosystem, the wider cybersecurity landscape, and Mehmet's view that security is above all a path of learning and exploration that never really ends.

We close on what makes Omarchy what it is — the innovation coming out of the community, and the excitement and engagement behind it.

Omarchy Stories — the podcast from the community, for the community.

Takeaways

  • Passion for cybersecurity from a young age
  • Impact of AI on vulnerability research Open source culture fosters contributions to the Linux ecosystem.
  • Vulnerability research in the Postgres ecosystem presents security challenges.
